The player moved one step along the dotted path toward the ball (from (53,10) to (51,12), the dot I clicked). So the mechanic is: click a dot on the path → the player moves to that dot (one step at a time, or to the clicked dot). The player moved from (53,10) to (51,12) — that's exactly the dot I clicked. And the dot I clicked turned into the player (G→p at (51,12)), and the old player position turned back into a dot (p→G at (53,10)). So the dots are "stepping stones," and the player moves to the clicked dot, leaving a dot behind.
Wait, actually the player moved to (51,12), and (53,10) became G (a dot) again. So the path dots are preserved, and the player is just riding on top of the path. The player can move to any clicked dot? Or only adjacent ones?
The player was at (53,10) and moved to (51,12). Those are adjacent dots on the path (consecutive). But earlier, the player moved from (58-60,3-5) to (53,10) — that was a big jump to the plus. So maybe the player can jump to any clicked dot, or maybe the plus was special.
Anyway, now I understand: click a dot → the player moves there. To reach the ball, I need to click the dots in sequence toward the ball. The dots from the player's position (51,12) toward the ball (17,46) are:
(49,14), (47,16), (45,18), (43,20), (41,22), (39,24), (37,26), (35,28), (33,30), (31,32), (29,34), (27,36), (25,38), (23,40), (21,42), (19,44), (17,46).
That's 17 more dots. But wait — can the player jump multiple dots at once, or does it have to be one at a time? Let me test: click a dot that's 2 steps away, e.g., (47,16) (skipping (49,14)). If the player moves there, it can jump. If it only moves to (49,14) or doesn't move, then it's one step at a time.
Actually, to be safe and efficient, let me think. If the player can jump to any dot, I can just click (17,46) (the last dot near the ball) and be done in 1 click. Let me test that: click (17,46). If the player moves there, great. If not, I'll go one at a time.
But wait, the ball is at (14-16, 47-49) (the gray core), and the last dot is at (17,46). The dot (17,46) is right next to the ball. So clicking (17,46) would bring the player right next to the ball. Then maybe one more click to the ball/core?
Actually, let me reconsider the goal. The goal is probably to get the player to the ball (or the gray core). Let me test the jump: click (17,46).
Let me reconsider: maybe the player can only move to adjacent dots. The first move was to the plus (special). The second move was to an adjacent dot. To determine if jumping is possible, let me test a non-adjacent dot.
Let me click (47,16) (2 steps away from the current (51,12)).
- If the player moves to (47,16): jumping is allowed → then click (17,46) to finish.
- If the player moves to (49,14) or doesn't move: one step at a time → click all dots in sequence.
Let me test (47,16).
Actually, to save steps, let me think about the most likely design. This looks like a "hop along the path" game. Usually, the player hops one dot at a time. But the first move was a big jump to the plus. Hmm, but the plus might have been a "goal marker" that the player was supposed to reach from the start (the start position was the corner, and the plus was the first target).
Let me just test the jump. Click (47,16).
